comment: The key miss was treating residual connections as an unconditional advantage and underweighting normalization/depth. On a 3-turn spiral at only 256 steps, the RMSprop .001 SiLU model B has the strongest progress. Among Adam-family candidates, the deep, heavily normalized plain ReLU model A handles the high-complexity boundary better than shallow D; low-rate C is slower, while E's residual zero-LN ReLU is especially poor. K1077/K1120 supported B, but K1020's zero-LN residual penalty and K1066's scoped deep-plus-more-LN preference were misapplied. The optimizer-only precedent q_3beb07 also had gold B<A<D<C<E.
hypothesis: For 3-turn two-spiral CE with T=256 and 16,384 samples, first select a high-progress RMSprop recipe (lr about 1e-3) when available. If comparing Adam/AdamW recipes, require normalized signal propagation for the deep boundary: a 5-layer plain ReLU network with 4/5 hidden LNs can beat shallower low-rate adaptive models. Residuals without sufficient LN are penalized; specifically, a 2-layer zero-LN residual ReLU at AdamW 1e-4 should rank below a 3-layer one-LN residual SiLU at Adam 3e-5, which itself ranks below a shallow 2-layer two-LN LeakyReLU at the same low rate. This rule is scoped to hard (3-turn) spirals and short budgets. Backtest: q_3beb07 (same optimizer-progress structure, shared normalized residual network) predicted B<A>D>C>E exactly; the present case is one additional exact hit, while q_fa7235/q_3eeb02 show that changing turns, rates, or architecture invalidates a universal order.

## Dataset
Synthetic tabular binary classification. Features are drawn i.i.d. from a standard normal; a latent score `s(x)` over a few active coordinates is thresholded at a fixed cut-off chosen near the median of `s(x)`, so the two classes are close to balanced. The score is non-linear in the features, so no linear function of the inputs reproduces the boundary. The dataset card below states the exact rule family, active coordinates, weights, threshold, and the class balance it produces. Every candidate trains on the same materialized train/test splits.

### Data-generating and classification rule
- Rule family: `piecewise_boundary`; active coordinates: `x_1`, `x_3`
- Feature distribution: every coordinate is sampled independently from `Normal(0, 1)`.
- Latent score:
  - If `x_1 > 0`: `s(x) = -1.375·x_3 - 1.375·x_1`
  - Otherwise: `s(x) = 0.875·x_3 - 1.375·x_1`
- Label rule: `y = 1` exactly when `s(x) > 0.125`; otherwise `y = 0`.
- Bayes decision boundary: `s(x) = 0.125`; labels are an exact function of `x`, so this boundary is attainable.
- Threshold calibration: `0.125` was chosen from 4096 independent calibration rows as the closest round value to the 50% quantile of `s(x)`; on those 4096 rows it labels 51.3% of them class 1.
- Reproducibility: point seed `4000495263426`, calibration seed `4000495264426`.

- Task: binary classification on one fixed synthetic tabular train/test split.
